verses.text: Then the Spirit led Jesus out into the wilderness, where the devil would test him.
Jesus fasted for forty days and forty nights. After all that, hunger hit hard.
The tempter came at him: “If you’re God’s Son, tell these stones to turn into bread.”
Jesus answered, “Scripture says, ‘A person doesn’t live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from God’s mouth.’”
Then the devil took him to the holy city and stood him on the temple’s highest point.
He said, “If you’re God’s Son, jump down. Scripture says, ‘He’ll command his angels to protect you,’ and, ‘They’ll catch you in their hands so you don’t even hit your foot on a stone.’”
Jesus answered him, “Scripture also says, ‘Don’t test the Lord your God.’”
Again, the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him every kingdom in the world and all its shine.
He said, “I’ll hand all this over if you bow down and worship me.”
Jesus told him, “Get out of here, Satan! Scripture says, ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve only him.’”
Then the devil left him, and angels came and cared for him.
When Jesus heard John had been arrested, he withdrew to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and made his home in Capernaum by the sea, in the regions of Zebulun and Naphtali.
That fulfilled what God had spoken through Isaiah the prophet:
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, by the sea, beyond the Jordan—Galilee where the nations live;”
“The people sitting in darkness have seen a great light. Light has dawned on those living in death’s shadow.” ✨
From then on, Jesus began preaching: “Turn back to God! The Kingdom of Heaven is right here.”
As Jesus walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers: Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew. They were fishermen, casting a net into the sea.
He told them, “Come with me, and I’ll teach you to fish for people.”
Right away, they left their nets and followed him.
Further along, he saw two other brothers—James, Zebedee’s son, and his brother John—in a boat with their father, Zebedee, fixing their nets. Jesus called them too.
They immediately left the boat and their father and followed Jesus.
Jesus traveled all over Galilee, teaching in the synagogues, announcing the Kingdom’s Good News, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.

News about him spread through all Syria. People brought him everyone who was sick or suffering from diseases and pain, people troubled by demons, people having seizures, and people who couldn’t move. Jesus healed them.
Huge crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and across the Jordan.
